purpose: Read-only pixel analysis; source images have not been edited. Rectangles are [x,y,width,height]. Aperture points are normalized to their own fixed-size source rectangle, not to the white-area bounding box.

registration.method: Shared medial tear-corner tip at local [302,140] pixels, with integer crop translation only. Width and height never change. Small painted changes in the lateral lid junction remain; no per-frame bbox fitting or image deformation is suggested.
registration.orientation: Outer lashes point left; pink medial tear corner is on the right. Mirror only when the destination eye requires the opposite orientation.
registration.closedAnchor: The closed frame has no pink tear corner, so its rightmost lower lash endpoint supplies the corresponding anchor. Happy-closed uses its pink tear-corner tip.
registration.destinationScale: Use a single uniform scale for all 12 rectangles; destination height = destination width * 0.6. Visible full feature spans about 274-289 source pixels. Destination width 130 produces a feature about 111-117 pixels wide. Do not fit each white-area bounding box to a destination.

profile.apertureMethod: Largest 4-connected white component per frame: alpha > 200, min(R,G,B) > 195, max(R,G,B)-min(R,G,B) < 24. Sampled 11 columns and inset within the visible white region, yielding 22 polygon points. Separate pale upper-lid highlights and tear-corner highlights are excluded. Closed/happy-closed deliberately have no aperture.
notes: Copy both the frame rectangle and aperture when adding quarter/threeQuarter/blink50 aliases to the renderer manifest; its gaze validation requires an aperture for every actual frame key.
Transparent pixels contain dark gray RGB and a few alpha 1-2 pixels. They are not an opaque gray backing. Do not use RGB alone to classify this asset as a solid background.

The open-to-first-intermediate white-area height drops from 92 to 69 source pixels, more than a precise 10% step. Later stages are progressively smaller. These are painted stages rather than equally spaced geometric closure; do not rescale to compensate.
The pale arc above the lash is painted eyelid highlight, not an iris aperture. Small pink skin/tear-corner edges are retained intentionally.
Pose names describe the visibly drawn shape: nearly circular, oblique ellipse, narrow vertical profile ellipse, wide low-angle ellipse. These are descriptive assignments, not image metadata.

Recommended rectangles add two source pixels of breathing room around alpha >= 32 bounds. A few almost invisible alpha 2 speckles extend farther and are intentionally excluded. No image has been trimmed or modified.
Keep each iris drawing at a fixed pose-specific size and translate it inside the corresponding aperture. Do not resize it as eye closure changes.
